skills.name: The sum of the angles of a triangle

note.text:
The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°. So the third angle is 180° minus the other two.
• In a right-angled triangle the two other angles add up to 90°.
• In an isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal.
• An exterior angle (made by extending a side) is equal to the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

check.prompt: In triangle ABC, Â = {a}° and Ĉ = {c}°. The side [AB] is extended beyond B. Find the exterior angle at B.

misconceptions.explain: That is the angle inside the triangle at B. The exterior angle is next to it: {a} + {c}.

solution: The exterior angle at B equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles, Â and Ĉ.

questions.prompt: A triangle has a right angle and an angle of {a}°. Find the third angle.

misconceptions.explain: Do not forget the right angle ({rt}°): {st} − {rt} − {a}.

solution: (The two other angles add up to {rt}°.)

questions.prompt: In an isosceles triangle the angle between the two equal sides is {a}°. Find each base angle.

misconceptions.explain: That is both base angles together. Divide by {2}.
The base angles are the two other angles, not the top one.

solution: The two base angles are equal and add up to {st} − {a} = {st - a}°.
